howto.name: Add the PDFs
howto.text: Drop or select one or more PDFs, up to 500 MB and 1,000 pages each. Each one is uploaded and converted on its own.

howto.name: Choose what the Markdown keeps
howto.text: Page markers put <!-- page 3 --> before each page, so you or an AI can cite pages; they don't show when the Markdown is displayed. Remove repeated headers and footers leaves out lines that repeat at the top or bottom of at least 40% of the pages, such as running titles and page numbers; a line whose only change is the page number counts as repeated. A line inside a table, or one that runs straight on into the text below it, stays. Both are on unless you switch them off.

howto.name: Split it into chunks (optional)
howto.text: One file is the default. By heading starts a new part at each heading of the two highest levels in the document; by size fills parts up to about 2,000 to 32,000 characters, ending each part between paragraphs, list items or table rows, and splitting only a paragraph or table too long for one part, between its sentences or rows. Take the parts as a ZIP of .md files, or as one .md file with <!-- chunk 2 of 7 --> between them.

howto.name: Convert and download
howto.text: Click Convert. The Markdown downloads by itself, and a single file can also be previewed and copied on the page. The result names any page without a text layer, which is left out, and the repeated lines that were removed.

faq.q: How do I convert a PDF to Markdown for ChatGPT, Claude or another LLM?
faq.a: Convert it here, then paste the Markdown into the chat or upload the .md file. LLM-ready means the Markdown keeps the structure a model reads a document by: headings by level, lists, tables as GitHub tables, code in fenced blocks and links with their addresses, without running headers, footers and page numbers breaking up the text. Page markers (<!-- page 3 -->) let the model say which page it is quoting, and chunks split a long document to fit an upload or context limit, or to load into a retrieval (RAG) index. To see how many tokens it uses, open AI Token Counter, then choose the downloaded .md file or paste the Markdown: it counts for GPT on your device, and for Claude or Gemini with your own API key, which sends the text to that provider.

Tables drawn with ruled lines become GitHub-flavoured Markdown tables, with a bold first row as the header row, and so do tables ruled only across: above, below and under their header, as LaTeX papers draw them, or only under their header and at their foot, as many invoices do. A cell whose text wraps stays one cell; Markdown cannot merge cells, so a merged cell's text sits in its first cell and the rest are left empty. A table laid out with spaces alone, with no lines at all, is not recognized as a table: each row comes out as a line of text, kept together.

faq.q: What about two-column papers and other multi-column layouts?
faq.a: Each column is usually read top to bottom before the next, and a title or table running across the columns is read in its place between them. Columns are found from the space between them, down to the 10-point gap of a LaTeX paper, in pages of two, three or four columns, justified or not, whichever way the file draws its text: a column at a time, or a line at a time across the page. One layout can still be read across: justified columns drawn a line at a time across, with a gap of 10 points or less. A paragraph that carries on into the next column usually stays whole; when it doesn't, it is split where the column ends, in the right order. Blocks side by side, such as the two addresses on an invoice, are read one after the other. A page whose text flows irregularly around pictures, or a title set beside a block of text, may still come out in a different order than you'd read it, so check the result.

faq.q: Can it convert a scanned PDF?
faq.a: Not directly. A scan holds pictures of the pages, with no text to read, so a PDF without any text is refused, and in a PDF that mixes both, each page without a text layer is named and left out. Run the scan through OCR PDF first: it adds a text layer, and the result converts here.

Each picture becomes a placeholder, [Image: ...], holding its alternative text when the PDF is tagged with one, or its caption when a line starting "Figure", "Fig." or the like sits right below or above it; otherwise just [Image]. Nothing is described or guessed, and small decorations such as logos are left out. Extract Images saves the pictures themselves.

faq.q: Are links, code and lists kept?
faq.a: Yes. Links to web and email addresses keep their targets as Markdown links; links that run scripts are dropped and their text kept. Text in a monospaced font becomes a fenced code block, indented as on the page, or inline code within a sentence, unless the whole document is set in one, as a printed text file is. Bulleted, numbered and lettered lists keep their nesting. The usual bullet shapes (•, ◦, ▪, –, ➢, ✓, ★, Word's Symbol and Wingdings bullets, and its "o" when set apart from the text) become Markdown's -, and numbers and letters stay; a mark it doesn't know, such as an emoji, stays in the text. Bold and italic text stays marked, and footnote marks and exponents become superscripts (<sup>).

faq.q: Does the Markdown include text I can't see in the PDF?
faq.a: It can. Like any text extraction, it takes the text in the file: white text, text too small to read and text covered by a box come through, while rotated text such as a diagonal watermark, and text outside the page, are left out. Before you give an AI the Markdown of a PDF someone else made, check it with the Hidden Text Checker for hidden instructions.

Yes. The conversion runs on the PrivaTools server, because it needs the position, font and size of every character and the lines drawn on each page. The file is uploaded over HTTPS, converted in isolated temporary per-request storage by a separate process with memory and CPU limits, and deleted with the Markdown once the result is sent; a background sweep clears anything an interrupted request leaves behind. Nothing is sent to an AI service, and the Markdown is not stored.

Up to 1,000 pages and 500 MB per PDF. The processing a file may use grows with its pages, 10 seconds plus 0.12 seconds a page and 60 seconds at most, which covers about 1,000 pages of plain text or several hundred pages with a table on each. A file that needs more is refused, and a conversion stops after 90 seconds in all; split a larger PDF with Split PDF and convert the parts. Password-protected PDFs must be unlocked first. As on the other heavy tools, one address can convert five PDFs a minute; in a bigger batch the rest say so and can be tried again a minute later.
